research_question: For each attested damaged, removed or missing body part of Horus, what caused the state, who caused it, how the part became displaced, who recovered it, who restored it, and what final restored state is actually stated?

evidence_levels.DIRECT_PRIMARY_TRANSLATION: The cited ancient text translation directly states the event or relation.
evidence_levels.DIRECT_PRIMARY_SEQUENCE_WITH_MOTIVE_UNST: The event is direct, but the actor's motive is not explicitly stated and must not be invented.
evidence_levels.CROSS_TEXT_VARIANT_LINK: A second ancient narrative supplies a plausible causal counterpart but is not identical to the first witness.
evidence_levels.SCHOLARLY_SYNTHESIS: Modern Egyptological synthesis connects variants; preserved separately from direct ancient wording.

source.title: Coffin Text 158 / Book of the Dead 113

direct_primary.initial_state: Horus's hands/arms are absent from their proper place and are scattered at the banks of the water.
direct_primary.causal_reference: The spell introduces the episode as something Horus's mother did to him, but the displayed UCL translation does not explicitly narrate the cutting action or contamination cause in the same passage.
direct_primary.retrieval_method: search/fishing and a snare or fish-trap
direct_primary.location: banks of the water / land of fishes
direct_primary.restoration_action: made them grow in their place

episodes.causal_ceiling: CT158/BD113 directly establishes displacement, retrieval and regrowth. It does not by itself fully spell out why the hands were severed or what contaminated them.

source.title: The Contendings of Horus and Seth, Papyrus Chester Beatty I
source.institution: Bibliotheca Alexandrina Digital Library of Inscriptions and Calligraphies

direct_primary.trigger: Seth sexually assaults Horus during the night and ejaculates between Horus's thighs.
direct_primary.contamination_event: Horus intercepts Seth's semen with his hands and shows it to Isis.
direct_primary.why_removed: The sequence directly places the cutting immediately after Isis sees Seth's semen in Horus's hands; removal is therefore contamination-linked in this narrative, although the translation does not add a modern medical explanation.

relation_to_CT158.reason: Chester Beatty I explicitly supplies the hand-cutting episode that CT158/BD113 leaves causally compressed. It is a later narrative witness and must not be silently inserted into CT158 as if both manuscripts said the same words.

source.title: The Contendings of Horus and Seth, Papyrus Chester Beatty I
source.institution: Bibliotheca Alexandrina Digital Library of Inscriptions and Calligraphies

direct_primary.preceding_context: Horus has beheaded Isis; the Ennead goes out to search for Horus to punish him.
direct_primary.damage_method: Seth seizes Horus, throws him down, removes both eyes from their sockets and buries them on the mountain.
direct_primary.motive: NOT_EXPLICITLY_STATED_AS_A_MOTIVE_BY_THE_TRANSLATION; the act occurs in the ongoing Horus-Seth conflict and punishment sequence.
direct_primary.displaced_eye_state: The two eyeballs become two bulbs that grow into lotuses.
direct_primary.treatment: gazelle milk applied to right and left eyes
direct_primary.verification: Hathor tells Horus to open his eyes, inspects them and finds them healed.
direct_primary.final_state: healed eyes / Horus restored to health

source.title: Coffin Text 335 / Book of the Dead 17, section 11

direct_primary.damage_state: Horus is injured and the wedjat-eye is damaged
direct_primary.paired_counter_action: Horus seizes the testicles of Seth
direct_primary.restoration_method: Thoth acts with his own fingers; a variant says the eye was ill from tears and Thoth spat upon it.

episodes.note: This witness establishes conflict-trauma and restoration but does not require complete physical extraction of the eye.

source.title: Coffin Text 157 / Book of the Dead 112

direct_primary.damage_agent: Seth in the form of a black boar
direct_primary.damage_method: a violent blow/burning strike of his arm in the eye of Horus
direct_primary.restoration_outcome: the gods declare Horus will be well

episodes.note: This is an eye-trauma variant, not an eye-loss witness.

source.author: Gyula Priskin
source.work: The Ancient Egyptian Book of the Moon: Coffin Texts Spells 154-160

scholarly_variant_synthesis.synthesis: Priskin reads CT158 in a lunar framework and links Horus's severed hands to the Isis/Seth-semen episode; the hands' placement in water and Sobek's fishing are interpreted as part of that mythic-lunar complex.
scholarly_variant_synthesis.critical_boundary: The contamination explanation and exact severing/throwing sequence must not be quoted as if explicitly narrated by the surviving CT158 wording when the primary translation is more compressed.

ordinary_tools_or_materials_attested: copper knife used by Isis in the hand-removal episode
snare/fish-trap used by Sobek in the hand-retrieval episode
gazelle milk used by Hathor in the eye-healing episode
Thoth's fingers and a spit variant in the wedjat restoration episode

requirements: Expand independently located Horus body-part damage/loss witnesses beyond hands and eyes.
For every witness freeze CAUSE, DAMAGE_AGENT, DAMAGE_METHOD, PART_STATE, DISPLACEMENT_LOCATION, RECOVERY_AGENT, RESTORATION_AGENT, RESTORATION_METHOD and FINAL_STATE separately.
Keep manuscript variants separate before constructing any merged causal graph.
Search head/face, torso/chest, legs/feet, bones/skin and falcon anatomy without borrowing Osiris body-part traditions unless explicitly linked to Horus.
Test whether cause class predicts restoration pathway better than organ identity alone.
Only after the causal graph is stable rerun the device-signature test.
